data.name: Lot
data.long_meaning: In the Hebrew Bible, Lot is the name of a nephew of Abraham and the father of the ancient cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. The name Lot may be derived from the Hebrew word 'lahatot' which means 'to cover'. Lot's name is a reminder of God's protection and provision for those who are outcast and in need.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of God's protection and provision for the outcast and in need.
data.numerology_meaning: Those with a 3 Life Path are adaptable, creative, and sociable. They have a natural talent for self-expression and artistic pursuits.

in_hebrew.name: לוט
in_hebrew.meaning: לוט: כיסוי, הסתרה, או נדודים במסע
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לוט הוא שם עברי שמקורו בשורש ל-ו-ט, שפירושו כיסוי, הסתרה, או נדודים במסע. במקרא, לוט הוא דמות חשובה המוזכרת בספר בראשית, ונקרא כך בשל נסיבות לידתו או בשל התכונות הרצויות לו. השם משקף את הרעיון של כיסוי או הגנה מפני פגעי העולם, והוא בעל חשיבות רבה במסורת היהודית והנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Λώτ
in_greek.long_meaning: Λώτ είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή λέξη לוט. Στη Βίβλο, ο Λώτ είναι μια σημαντική προσωπικότητα που αναφέρεται στο βιβλίο της Γένεσης. Το όνομα Λώτ σημαίνει κάλυμμα ή προστασία, αντανακλώντας την προστασία που έλαβε από τον Θεό κατά την καταστροφή της Σοδόμης και της Γομόρρας. Στην παλαιοχριστιανική παράδοση, ο Λώτ θεωρείται πρότυπο πιστού που αντιμετωπίζει προκλήσεις με πίστη.

in_latin.name: Lot
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lot in lingua Latina est translatio nominis Hebraici לוט. In Scriptura Sacra, Lot est figura quae in libro Genesis apparet. Nomen significat velamen seu tegmen, reflectens protectionem divinam quam Lot experitur in sua vita, praesertim durante destructione Sodomae et Gomorrae. In traditione christiana primitiva, Lot habetur exemplum fidelitatis in adversis.

in_english.name: Lot
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lot originates from the Hebrew word לוט, meaning covering, protection, or traveler. In the Bible, Lot is a significant figure mentioned in the book of Genesis. The name reflects the idea of divine protection, as seen in Lot's rescue from the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. In Christian tradition, Lot is considered an example of faithfulness and divine providence. The name has been used across various Christian cultures, symbolizing shelter and guidance.

biblical_reference.note: Lot is the nephew of Abraham and is known for his journey and experiences in Sodom and Gomorrah.

data.cultural_impact: The biblical story of Lot and his connection to the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah has had a profound impact on Western culture. These cities are often used as metaphors for places of moral depravity and wickedness. Lot's name and story have been referenced in literature, art, and music, often with a negative connotation.
data.spiritual_significance: Despite the negative associations with Lot's name in culture, spiritually, he serves as a reminder of God's faithfulness and protection. Even in the midst of a society that was traditionally considered wicked and immoral, Lot and his family were saved from destruction by God. The story of Lot is a testament to the fact that even in the darkest of places, God's provision and protection are still present.

historical_references.reference:
Lot is mentioned in the Book of Genesis as a nephew of Abraham and the father of the ancient cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. He is described as a righteous man who lived in the cities surrounded by wicked people.

Genesis 13:12-13: 'So Abram settled in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived among the cities of the Plain and moved his tent as far as Sodom.'

Lot is also known from the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text that is not part of the Hebrew Bible. In this text, Lot is described as the father of Moab and Ammon, who are considered the ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites. It is believed that this text was written between the 3rd and 1st centuries BCE.

Book of Enoch 19:1-3: 'And Lot the son of Abram went towards the east, and they separated from him. And Lot dwelt in the plain in the east, and his two sons were born unto him in the land of Sodom: the name of the elder was Moab, and the name of the younger was Ammon.'

trends: Biblical character in Abrahamic faiths, represented as a righteous man who was chosen by God to save his family from destruction
In pop culture, Lot is often portrayed as a drunken, effeminate man, or a symbol of Sodom and Gomorrah's depravity
platforms: Literature: In works such as D.H. Lawrence's 'Lady Chatterley's Lover' and E.M. Forster's 'Maurice', Lot is used as a symbol for homosexuality and same-sex love

Comics: In Marvel Comics' 'Fantastic Four', Reed Richards renames his spaceship 'Lot's Car' as a reference to the biblical story of Lot's wife turning into a pillar of salt when she disobeyed God's warning not to look back
Video Games: In 'The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim', Lot is mentioned as the father of a character, and his name is used as a reference for a location in the game 'Hammerfell'
modern_usage.modern_context: Lot is often used as a symbol for the consequences of unchecked depravity, as seen in the biblical story of Sodom and Gomorrah. However, in modern pop culture, he is also depicted as a drunken, effeminate man or a symbol of homosexuality and same-sex love. This contrast shows the complex and nuanced ways in which religious and secular narratives intersect and influence one another in modern society.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Lot from New York, United States embodies the meaning of Lot - "Fugitive, outcast, refugee". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Lot signifies separation, representing the biblical figure who was chosen but chose to live in the sinful cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, ultimately leading to his devastating separation from God and his family. Overcoming Lot's narrative involves recognizing the importance of choosing righteousness and separating oneself from sin.
